reason: The cited evidence shows that SRO exists in HEAs (E1) and that compositional complexity promotes homogeneous flow by impeding dislocation glide (E3), but none of the passages addresses SRO at multilayer interfaces, its disruption under sustained load, or its effect on creep. The key premises about interfacial SRO and its role in creep are therefore unsupported by the provided citations.
premises: Interfaces in HEA nanoscale multilayers possess chemical short-range order (SRO).
Interfacial SRO impedes dislocation motion, raising local energy barriers.
Under sustained load, local stress can disrupt interfacial SRO.
SRO disruption lowers barriers, enabling dislocation glide and diffusion-assisted creep.
Enhancing interfacial SRO by annealing delays creep onset and leads to more gradual plastic flow.
